seal.statement: A change to a file under a full-corpus trigger directory that does not define the push gate is proved by its own cone, not by the whole corpus; the trigger directories stay fail-closed. The two directory rules of FULL_CORPUS_TRIGGER_RULES (selection-state: test/manifests/; push-gate: .githooks/) stay, so any file under them - a new one included - still runs the whole corpus, and each rule exempts by name exactly the files proven not to define the gate, each exemption carrying a one-line reason naming its only consumers. A file is proven not to define the gate only when nothing the gate runs names it (the files that trip a trigger, the package scripts they run through npm, transitively, and the import closure of every script they name) and a test observes it by name in the observation census; an exemption is witnessed to fail when either stops holding. Witnessed on the real selection through buildExecutionPlan and decidePushProof: a change to test/manifests/pre-push-stages.json (the incident: a ~40-minute full corpus for a file read only by the apparatus budget, whose 179-test cone already held both its observers) and to every other exempted file runs the change proof with its named observers in the cone; a change to the post-push manifest, proof-obligations.json, the safety spine, the impact contracts, .githooks/pre-push, any unexempted file under a trigger directory, or a new unlisted file under test/manifests/ or .githooks/ runs the whole corpus. .githooks/pre-push itself stays a trigger (dropping it is an owner decision not made here). No script, workflow or gate is added or weakened.

Any new file under test/manifests/ or .githooks/ triggers by default.

Sibling census (recorded, nothing narrowed): (1) subsystem widening - the selector maps test/(shards|manifests)/ (source-shard-manifests) and .githooks/ (source-repo-config) to the test-infrastructure subsystem, so an exempted file's cone is 158-180 tests (the 179 of the incident). Narrowing to named observers is NOT proven safe: the observation census sees only literal paths in test sources, and tests reach these manifests through imported constants too (acceptance-proof-manifest-runner.test.js reads the smoke manifest by literal, but a test could import a path constant), so the subsystem widening is the backstop; same owner (selector taxonomy) but different mechanism - left. (2) .githooks/pre-push:327-334 relints the whole tree on ANY byte change to eslint.config.js, package.json or package-lock.json, including a version-only bump or a scripts-field edit; the lint verdict depends on the config and the eslint plugin set, not the version field, so keying it on the semantic lockfile graph (select-change-tests.js lockfileDependencyGraph) plus the devDependencies would be narrower, but it is the lint stage's owner and a different mechanism (and eslint --cache bounds the cost) - left; same class as census P-E. (3) package.json/package-lock.json: not corpus triggers; the selector already masks the version (lockfileDependencyGraph) - correct. (4) test-config (.taprc), test-placement (scripts/lab/probe|process|state.js), gate-scheduler, selection-machinery and test-runner are file-level rules, each covered by the existing import-closure witness - correct as is. (5) run-static-audits wholeTree obligations (audit:no-kiro, audit:no-legacy-naming) are whole-tree by design (census of literals). No other directory-keyed 'changed X => everything' rule exists in FULL_CORPUS_TRIGGER_RULES.
